title: My God, My Life, My Love
description: My God, My Life, My Love in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 93, headed “God all, and in all, Psalm 73. 25”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, my life, my love, To thee, to thee I call, I can-not live if thou re-move, For thou art all in all.

lines: My God, my life, my love,
To thee, to thee I call,
I cannot live if thou remove,
For thou art all in all.
'Tis heaven to rest in thine embrace,
And no where else but there.
They sit around thy gracious throne,
Nor earth nor all the sky
No not a drop of real joy,
Thou art the sea of love,
The circle where my passions move,
And yet how far from thee I lie!

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
